```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)   # template only: set eval = TRUE once packages and data are installed
```

The function calls below come from:

* each package's tutorial, and
* the wrappers in the anchor benchmark's official repo, [weiqi-grace-li/ctsvg-benchmark](https://github.com/weiqi-grace-li/ctsvg-benchmark) (`method_wrappers/*.R`). That repo also pins exact versions in `renv.lock`: CELINA 1.0, STANCE 0.3.0, spVC 0.1.0, spacexr 2.2.1, CTSV 1.12.0, MCube 0.0.0.9000.

The quickest way to get a working environment identical to the benchmark's:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/weiqi-grace-li/ctsvg-benchmark.git
cd ctsvg-benchmark
Rscript -e 'install.packages("renv"); renv::restore()'
```

# 0. Install

```{r install}
install.packages(c("devtools", "BiocManager"))
BiocManager::install(c("SpatialExperiment", "CTSV", "imcdatasets", "Statial", "scDesign3"))
devtools::install_github("pekjoonwu/CELINA")        # CELINA (Shang, Wu, Zhou 2025)
devtools::install_github("Cui-STT-Lab/STANCE")      # STANCE (Su et al. 2025)
devtools::install_github("dmcable/spacexr")         # RCTD + C-SIDE (Cable et al. 2022)
devtools::install_github("FIRST-Data-Lab/BPST")     # spVC dependency
devtools::install_github("FIRST-Data-Lab/Triangulation")
devtools::install_github("shanyu-stat/spVC")        # spVC (Yu & Li 2024)
devtools::install_github("YangLabHKUST/MCube")      # MMM / MCube
devtools::install_github("haotian-zhuang/findPC")
devtools::install_github("haotian-zhuang/ctSVG")    # ctSVG (Zhuang et al. 2025)
```

# 1. Get the inputs every method needs

Every ctSVG method takes the same four things:

| Object | Shape | Spatial proteomics source |
|---|---|---|
| `counts` | features × locations | marker intensities (IMC/MIBI/CODEX) **or** antibody UMI counts (Visium CytAssist protein) |
| `pos` / `coords` | locations × 2 | cell centroids (x, y) or spot coordinates |
| `comp` / `prop` / `W` | locations × K | **one-hot** cell-type matrix for single-cell data; deconvolved proportions for spots |
| (optional) scRNA reference | — | needed only by CELINA preprocessing and RCTD-based tools (C-SIDE, MMM) |

## Route A: single-cell multiplexed imaging (Keren 2018 MIBI, `kerenSCE`)

```{r route-a}
library(Statial); library(SingleCellExperiment)
data("kerenSCE")
img <- kerenSCE[, kerenSCE$imageID == unique(kerenSCE$imageID)[1]]   # one image at a time

expr   <- assay(img, "intensities")                     # markers x cells (continuous)
coords <- as.matrix(colData(img)[, c("x", "y")])
rownames(coords) <- colnames(img)
ctype  <- factor(img$cellType)
comp   <- model.matrix(~ ctype - 1)                     # cells x K one-hot
colnames(comp) <- levels(ctype); rownames(comp) <- colnames(img)

# Most ctSVG tools assume counts. Two pragmatic options for intensities:
#  (i)  pseudo-counts: round(expr * scale_factor). Simple, but violates the count model.
#  (ii) use the methods that accept normalized data (STANCE normalized = TRUE)
#       or the Gaussian-friendly baselines in ../02_global_SVG_methods.
counts_pseudo <- round(pmax(expr, 0) * 100)

# Exclude lineage markers that were used to DEFINE each cell type when testing within that type.
lineage_markers <- c("CD3", "CD4", "CD8", "CD20", "CD68", "Keratin6", "Pan-Keratin", "Vimentin", "CD45")
```

## Route B: spot-level protein counts (10x Visium CytAssist Gene + Protein)

```{r route-b}
x <- Seurat::Read10X_h5("datasets/raw/10x/tonsil/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
rna  <- x[["Gene Expression"]]
prot <- x[["Antibody Capture"]]                          # 35 antibodies, integer UMI counts
pos  <- read.csv("datasets/raw/10x/tonsil/spatial/tissue_positions.csv", row.names = 1)
pos  <- as.matrix(pos[colnames(prot), c("pxl_col_in_fullres", "pxl_row_in_fullres")])
colnames(pos) <- c("x", "y")

# Cell-type proportions from the RNA modality with RCTD (needs a tonsil scRNA-seq reference)
library(spacexr)
ref   <- Reference(sc_counts, sc_types)                  # sc_counts: genes x cells; sc_types: named factor
puck  <- SpatialRNA(as.data.frame(pos), rna)
rctd  <- run.RCTD(create.RCTD(puck, ref, max_cores = 4), doublet_mode = "full")
comp  <- as.matrix(normalize_weights(rctd@results$weights))   # spots x K
# Then pass `prot` as the counts matrix to the methods below.
```

# 2. CELINA: random-effect spatially varying coefficient model, 11 kernels

```{r celina}
library(CELINA)
obj <- Create_Celina_Object(celltype_mat = t(comp),          # K x locations
                            gene_expression_mat = counts,    # features x locations
                            location = coords,
                            covariates = NULL, project = "BIOINF590")
obj <- preprocess_input(obj,
                        cell_types_to_test = colnames(comp),
                        scRNA_count = sc_count,              # reference used for its gene QC filter
                        sc_cell_type_labels = as.factor(sc_type),
                        threshold = 5e-5)                    # benchmark warns: this QC can drop true signals
obj <- Calculate_Kernel(obj, approximation = ncol(counts) > 8000,
                        sparseKernel = TRUE, sparseKernel_tol = 1e-4)
obj <- Testing_interaction_all(obj, celltype_to_test = colnames(comp), num_cores = 4)
celina_res <- obj@result                                     # list by cell type; column "CombinedPvals"
```

# 3. STANCE: linear mixed model, two-stage test (rotation-invariant)

```{r stance}
library(STANCE)
st <- creatSTANCEobject(counts = counts, pos = coords, prop = comp, covariates = NULL)
st <- data_preprocess(st, gene.threshold = 0.05, spot.threshold = 10, normalized = FALSE)
st <- build_kernelMatrix(st)
st <- runTest1(st, correction = FALSE, pv.adjust = "BY")         # stage 1: overall SVG test
svg <- rownames(st@gene_expression)[st@Test_1$p_value_adj < 0.05]
st <- runTest2(st, Genes_to_test = svg, Cell_types_to_test = NULL,
               correction = FALSE, ncores = 4)                   # stage 2: per-cell-type test
head(st@Test_2[[colnames(comp)[1]]])
st <- CT_topGenes(st, CT_of_interest = colnames(comp)[1], numTopGenes = 20)
visualizeGenePattern(st, gene_to_display = svg[1])
# Benchmark caveat: STANCE has no constant cross-cell-type effect, so it tends to call markers ctSVGs.
```

# 4. C-SIDE (spacexr): fixed effects + splines, on RCTD

```{r cside}
library(spacexr)
puck <- SpatialRNA(as.data.frame(coords), counts)
ref  <- Reference(sc_counts, sc_types, colSums(sc_counts), min_UMI = 25)
rctd <- create.RCTD(spatialRNA = puck, ref, max_cores = 4)
rctd <- import_weights(rctd, comp)                 # use known one-hot types / deconvolved proportions
rctd@config$RCTDmode <- "full"
rctd <- run.CSIDE.nonparam(rctd, df = 15, cell_types = NULL, gene_threshold = 5e-5,
                           cell_type_threshold = 125, fdr = 0.05, doublet_mode = FALSE,
                           weight_threshold = 0.8)
cside_res <- rctd@de_results$all_gene_list         # per cell type
```

# 5. CTSV: ZINB with x/y kernels, Cauchy combination

```{r ctsv}
library(CTSV); library(SpatialExperiment); library(BiocParallel)
spe <- SpatialExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts), spatialCoords = coords)
res <- CTSV(spe, comp, num_core = 4, BPPARAM = MulticoreParam(workers = 4))
# res$pval / res$qval are G x 2K (columns 1..K = x-axis kernels, K+1..2K = y-axis kernels)
sv  <- svGene(res$qval, 0.05)
sv$SVGene                                           # list of ctSV features per cell type
# Fixed x/y bases mean results are NOT rotation-invariant (see ctSVGbench rotation tests).
```

# 6. spVC: generalized Poisson with spatially varying coefficients over a triangulation

```{r spvc}
library(spVC); library(BPST); library(Triangulation); library(MGLM)
# Tissue boundary: draw interactively with identify(), or use the convex hull for a TMA core
hull     <- coords[chull(coords), ]
Tr.cell  <- TriMesh(hull, n = 2)
spvc     <- test.spVC(Y = counts, X = comp, S = coords,
                      V = as.matrix(Tr.cell$V), Tr = as.matrix(Tr.cell$Tr),
                      para.cores = 4, filter.min.nonzero = 100)
# results.constant: constant effects; results.varying: genes with spatially varying effects.
# p.value entries named gamma_<celltype> are the cell-type-specific spatial tests.
spvc$results.varying[[1]]$p.value
```

# 7. MMM (MCube): the sixth method in the official benchmark repo

```{r mmm}
library(MCube); library(spacexr)
rctd <- create.RCTD(SpatialRNA(as.data.frame(coords), counts, colSums(counts)),
                    Reference(sc_counts, sc_types, colSums(sc_counts), min_UMI = 25), max_cores = 4)
mc <- createMCube(counts = t(counts), coordinates = coords, proportions = comp,
                  library_sizes = colSums(counts),
                  reference = t(rctd@cell_type_info$info[[1]]),
                  used_for_deconvolution = rownames(rctd@spatialRNA@counts),
                  spot_effects = log(rowSums(comp)), platform_effect = NULL,
                  proportion_threshold = 0.1, celltype_threshold = 100, reference_threshold = 0.5)
mc <- mcubeFitNull(mc, num_workers = 4, num_threads = 1)
mc <- mcubeTest(mc, num_workers = 4, num_threads = 1, shared_memory = TRUE)
mc@pvalues                                          # per cell type; column "combined_pvalue"
```

# 8. ctSVG (Zhuang et al.): built for single-cell-resolution data (Visium HD / Xenium)

Closest in spirit to multiplexed imaging: cells → clusters → B-spline spatial model **within each cluster** → permutation null.
Check the vignettes ("Apply ctSVG to Xenium data") at <https://haotian-zhuang.github.io/ctSVG/> for the current function names, then plug in `expr`, `coords`, `ctype` from Route A.

```{r ctsvg}
library(ctSVG)
?ctSVG          # see the reference index for the main entry point and its arguments
```

# 9. Harmonise outputs for evaluation

Turn every result into a long table with the columns `method, cell_type, feature, p_value`, then run `../05_evaluation_framework/metrics.py`. The benchmark repo's `*_details_save()` functions show how to reshape each method's output. A feature a method did not test gets `p_value = -1`. That matters, because QC filters that silently drop features are one of the benchmark's key findings.

```{r harmonise}
to_long <- function(lst, pcol, method) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(lst), function(ct)
    data.frame(method = method, cell_type = ct, feature = rownames(lst[[ct]]),
               p_value = lst[[ct]][, pcol])))
}
long <- rbind(to_long(celina_res, "CombinedPvals", "CELINA"),
              to_long(mc@pvalues, "combined_pvalue", "MMM"))
long$p_adj <- p.adjust(long$p_value, "BH")
write.csv(long, "results_ctsv_long.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
